QuestionText: A ________ is a person who belongs to a country and has certain rights and duties.
Explanation: Citizens are members of a community or country who work together to make it better.

QuestionText: Why does a school have rules?
Options: B) To keep students safe and help them learn
C) To stop people from talking
D) To keep the lights on
Explanation: Rules provide order and ensure everyone is treated fairly and stays safe.

QuestionText: Rules that are made by the government for everyone in a country to follow are called ________.
Explanation: Laws are official rules that help protect people's rights and safety.

QuestionText: Which of these is a way to be a good citizen?
Explanation: Good citizens follow laws, help others, and take care of their environment.

QuestionText: What do we call a choice that is made by a group of people after counting their preferences?
Explanation: Voting is a fair way for a group to make a decision together.

QuestionText: The group of people who lead a city, state, or country is called the ________.
Explanation: The government makes laws and provides services like schools and roads.

QuestionText: Who is the head of a city's local government?
Explanation: The Mayor is the leader of a city or town.

QuestionText: In a democracy, who chooses the leaders of the government?
Explanation: Democracy means 'rule by the people,' where citizens vote for their leaders.

QuestionText: Which of these is a 'right' that a child has?
Options: A) To eat candy for every meal
B) To go to school and get an education
D) To never clean their room
Explanation: Rights are things you are allowed to be, do, or have to stay safe and healthy.

QuestionText: Which of these is a 'responsibility' of a student?
Explanation: A responsibility is something you are expected to do.

QuestionText: What does a 'Fair' rule mean?
Options: A) It only helps the teacher
B) It applies to everyone equally
D) It is hard to follow
Explanation: Fairness means treating everyone the same way under the same rules.

QuestionText: Who is the current Prime Minister of India? (As of early 2026)
Explanation: Narendra Modi has been the Prime Minister since 2014.

QuestionText: Which building is the workplace of the President of India?
Explanation: Rashtrapati Bhavan is the official home and office of the President.

QuestionText: A ________ is a promise made by a citizen to be loyal to their country.
Explanation: Pledges, like the National Pledge of India, show respect for the nation.

QuestionText: Which of these is a service provided by the government?
Explanation: Governments use tax money to provide services that help everyone.

QuestionText: What happens if someone breaks a law?
Options: B) They may face a consequence (like a fine or jail)
D) They make a new law
Explanation: Consequences help people understand that following laws is important.

QuestionText: Who is the current President of India? (As of early 2026)
Explanation: Droupadi Murmu is the 15th President of India.

QuestionText: The set of rules by which a country is governed is called the ________.
Explanation: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land.

QuestionText: Which animal is shown on the National Emblem of India?
Explanation: The emblem features four lions standing back-to-back.

QuestionText: What is the minimum age to vote in India?
Explanation: Every citizen who is 18 years or older has the right to vote.

QuestionText: True or False: Only grown-ups can be good citizens.
Explanation: Children can be good citizens by helping others and following rules at school.

QuestionText: Which branch of government makes the laws?
Explanation: In India, the Parliament (Sansad) is where new laws are discussed and passed.

QuestionText: What do we call a person who leads a state government in India?
Explanation: Each state in India has a Chief Minister (CM) as its leader.

QuestionText: Which of these is a way to solve a disagreement peacefully?
Options: B) Talking and listening to each other
Explanation: Communication helps people understand different points of view.

QuestionText: What is the capital city of India?
Explanation: New Delhi is the seat of the central government of India.

QuestionText: Who helps the judge in a courtroom to decide if a law was broken?
Explanation: Lawyers present evidence to help the court make a fair decision.

QuestionText: Which of these is a symbol of our country's government?
Explanation: The flag represents the nation and its government.

QuestionText: What do we call the place where people go to cast their votes?
Explanation: Citizens go to polling stations during an election to vote.

QuestionText: Why is it important to tell the truth in a community?
Options: A) So people will trust you
C) To make the day go faster
D) Because it is a secret
Explanation: Trust and honesty are key parts of being a good citizen.

QuestionText: The 'Preamble' is the ________ to the Constitution.
Explanation: The Preamble explains the goals and values of the Constitution.

QuestionText: Which of these is a responsibility you have toward the environment?
Explanation: Taking care of the Earth is a global responsibility for all citizens.

QuestionText: Who protects the country's borders?
Options: B) The Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force)
Explanation: The military keeps the country safe from outside threats.

QuestionText: What does 'Equality' mean in a community?
Options: A) Everyone gets exactly the same toy
B) Everyone has the same rights and opportunities
C) Everyone must wear the same clothes
D) Everyone must eat the same food
Explanation: Equality means no one is treated better or worse because of who they are.

QuestionText: Which of these is a rule for safety on the road?
Options: B) Run across when the light is red
C) Play ball in the street
Explanation: Traffic rules like wearing seatbelts save lives.

QuestionText: What is the name of the paper or electronic screen used for voting?
Explanation: A ballot is used to record a person's vote.

QuestionText: Who makes sure that the laws are being followed by citizens?
Explanation: Law enforcement officers work to keep the community safe and orderly.

QuestionText: What does 'Veto' mean?
Options: A) To agree with a law
B) To say 'no' to a law or decision
C) To write a new law
Explanation: A veto is a power used by leaders to stop an official action.

QuestionText: Which of these is a quality of a good leader?
Explanation: Good leaders listen, help others, and are fair.

QuestionText: A ________ is a group of people who make laws for a state or country.
Explanation: Legislative bodies like councils and parliaments debate and pass laws.

QuestionText: Why do we pay taxes to the government?
Options: A) To buy gifts for the leaders
B) To pay for public services like roads and schools
D) Because we want to give it away
Explanation: Taxes provide the money needed for things that benefit the whole community.

QuestionText: Which of these is an example of 'Volunteering'?
Options: A) Getting paid to wash a car
B) Helping at a food bank for free
C) Selling toys at a store
Explanation: Volunteers give their time to help the community without being paid.

QuestionText: What is the national motto of India?
Explanation: Satyameva Jayate means 'Truth Alone Triumphs'.

QuestionText: The President of India is elected for a term of ________ years.
Explanation: The President serves a five-year term.

QuestionText: Which of these is a way to show respect for the National Flag?
Options: A) Letting it touch the ground
B) Standing at attention when it is raised
D) Using it as a tablecloth
Explanation: Showing respect for the flag is a way of showing respect for the country.

QuestionText: True or False: Every country in the world has the same laws.
Explanation: Each country makes its own laws based on its needs and values.

QuestionText: A person who is chosen to speak for a larger group of people is a ________.
Explanation: Representatives are elected to voice the opinions of the citizens in government.

QuestionText: What do we call the official rules of a game?
Explanation: Rules in games make sure everyone plays fairly and has fun.

QuestionText: Which of these is a service provided by the local post office?
Explanation: Post offices are part of a government-run communication system.

QuestionText: What does 'Justice' mean?
Options: B) Being treated fairly and according to the law
Explanation: Justice ensures that people are treated fairly and that their rights are protected.

QuestionText: Which document starts with the words 'We, the People of India'?
Explanation: These opening words show that the power of the country comes from its citizens.
